main_issue: Whether Agent D can keep cooking strong-smelling salted fish in the shared kitchen, and what rule or arrangement could address the smell affecting A, B and C.

A-B.evidence: B backs A: 'He's right. It's not like other cooking' (8); 'It's a problem for more than just one person' (15); A accepts B's objection that Saturdays won't work (22, 24).

A-C.evidence: C complains about laundry smell (3) and rejects the Saturday idea (23); A concedes 'Saturdays won't work' (24). Both want the smell problem solved.

A-D.evidence: D resists restriction ('It's a kitchen. People cook here' 6; 'So because there are three of you, I cannot cook?' 16); A offers Saturdays (19), D objects (20); no agreement and A asks for other ideas (24).

B-C.evidence: B says the day makes no difference because of laundry (22); C replies 'Yeah, she's right' (23).

B-D.evidence: B says it sticks to fabrics (8) and is a problem for more than one person (15), prompting D's 'So because there are three of you, I cannot cook?' (16). D cites laundry against Saturdays (20), which B uses (22).

C-D.evidence: C complains about laundry (3), D defends the dish (4). D raises the laundry objection to Saturdays (20) and C confirms it (23), but D still opposes any ban.
